text: {"summary": "Ratan Tata, chairman of the Tata Group, said he feels lonely and in pain because of newspaper attacks on his reputation during his ongoing power struggle with Cyrus Mistry and Nusli Wadia. He spoke at the Tata Chemicals shareholders' meeting, where shareholders backed him, and he thanked them for their support."}

{"summary": "The post teases the article's list of 11 great 2016 movies streaming on Netflix plus one on Hulu, with the Hulu pick being Whiskey Tango Foxtrot, starring Tina Fey as a journalist covering the Afghanistan war. Other picks include The Jungle Book, The Invitation, 13th, and Barry, a biopic of Obama's college years."}

{"summary": "The writer, a heavy phone user, switched from his beloved Galaxy S7 to an iPhone 6s Plus because the S7 died around 5 p.m. daily, while the iPhone's better-optimized software lasts much longer despite having a smaller battery."}

{"summary": "About 40 people were burned at a Tony Robbins seminar in Dallas during a hot-coal firewalking exercise, the same kind of incident that happened in San Jose in 2012. The post teases a 'dumbest reason,' which the article says is lingering too long on the coals, often to take selfies, rather than walking at a steady pace on properly burned-down coals."}

{"summary": "Scientists worry that Finding Dory could spark a pet-trade boom for blue tang fish, as Finding Nemo did for clownfish. Blue tangs are rarer, don't do well in tanks, and are collected from Indonesia and the Philippines with few regulations, risking damage to ecosystems."}

{"summary": "The post teases that fashion designer Charlotte Ronson's New York City home is surprisingly down-to-earth rather than lavish. The article says her airy, white-walled apartment, shown on Domaine Home, is filled with eclectic artwork, bright touches like baby blue dining chairs, and fresh flowers."}

{"summary": "The post teases a list of 29 powerful pieces of writing by women from 2016, curated by a publication for its fifth year. The article is that list, covering topics like Hillary Clinton's nomination, Black Lives Matter, abortion, sexual assault, and Trump's election, with a short blurb and link for each piece."}

{"summary": "The post teases that the latest show canceled this season is CBS's sitcom \"We Are Men,\" which was pulled after weak ratings. CBS is replacing it with \"2 Broke Girls\" at 8:30 p.m. ET from Oct. 14, and \"Mike and Molly\" returns to its 9 p.m. slot on Nov. 4."}

{"summary": "The food industry has announced plans to make product labels easier to understand by using clearer language, with the changes expected to reach grocery store shelves soon. The post is teasing that food labels will be rewritten in plainer wording to reduce confusion."}

{"summary": "ScHoolboy Q revealed he almost quit rap after his sophomore album Oxymoron, taking about three years of breaks that cost him time raising his daughter, now seven. He said he won't put music and money above family, so fans worry he may eventually step away from hip-hop."}

{"summary": "The post teases a list of 19 teens doing quirky or memorable things in 2016, like a Mulan-themed ID photo, an umbrella shower pic, a deer named Money, and a teen who found a dead body while playing Pokemon Go. It's a lighthearted roundup of viral teen stunts, pranks, and oddball moments."}

{"summary": "The post teases a hidden detail in John Carpenter's The Thing: cinematographer Dean Cundey says he and Carpenter added a subtle \"eye light\", a small gleam in the eyes of human characters, so viewers can tell who is still human and not the shape-shifting Thing. The article notes this was revealed in a commentary for a new Scream Factory Blu-ray and invites viewers to check the ending to see if the last two men standing are human."}

{"summary": "The post teases New Zealand's most complained-about company, which is telco Spark, with 140 complaints to the Commerce Commission in its 2016 Consumer Issues Paper. Vodafone (133) and Trade Me sellers (121) followed, and pricing was the most common complaint issue, though complaints don't necessarily mean illegal conduct."}

{"summary": "Men are using period-tracking apps like iAmAMan and uPMS to monitor female colleagues' and partners' menstrual cycles, to avoid their moods during PMS. One woman said coworkers tracked her cycle after an argument, and the public widely criticized the practice as creepy."}

{"summary": "Amy Cazin, a former stay-at-home mom who started Primal Pit Paste with $100, turned down a Wal-Mart offer to sell her natural deodorant because she wasn't yet ready to supply such a large retailer. Her company now sells through Whole Foods and independent retailers, with sales doubling yearly."}

{"summary": "Bikers Bret and Zach Winingar found an emaciated, locked-in dog inside a chewed-up animal crate while riding near Little Rock, Arkansas. They rescued her, named her Charlie Bravo (CB), and took her to a vet. She recovered into a healthy pup, and donations are funding a new charity called C.B's Angels."}

{"summary": "The post teases McLaren's cost: about £1 billion ($1.45 billion) over six years on R&D to launch 15 new cars by 2022, including a P1 successor, with new powertrains, hybrids, carbon fiber structures, and possibly an all-electric model. It aims to grow sales from 2,000 to 5,000 supercars a year, per CEO Mike Flewitt."}

{"summary": "The post teases that robots and smart home gadgets fail to transform homes because they add little value and struggle in chaotic, nonstandard environments. The article, using Roomba and Nest as examples, notes that a Roomba spread dog poop across an Arkansas man's house, that these devices get stuck and save little time, and that preinternet appliances are already good enough."}

{"summary": "The post teases bone broth, a slow-cooked soup made from simmered beef or chicken bones with vegetables, apple cider vinegar, and herbs. Health experts praise it as a morning drink for bone, skin, and digestive health, and the article includes a full recipe."}

{"summary": "Amateur archaeologists in Tivoli, Italy, uncovered a new underground passageway beneath Emperor Hadrian's second-century villa, leading from the Academy area to a 2.5-mile roadway called the Grande Trapezio. The tunnels were likely used by slaves, merchants, and carts to supply the estate unseen, though their exact purpose remains unclear."}

{"summary": "The post teases a big Rockstar announcement for GTA 6, but the article is satire, not news. It mocks rumored leaks: no confirmed release date, a protagonist-driven story, improved graphics and AI, no PS1 or N64 release, and absurd shop names and microtransactions."}

{"summary": "The post teases why Indian fans usually have 3 blades while US fans have 4. The article explains that US fans with 4 blades are designed to move a large mass of air slowly, supplementing air conditioning, while Indian 3-blade fans are lighter, spin faster, and provide convective cooling on their own while being energy efficient."}

{"summary": "Whole Foods co-CEO Walter Robb says the trait that will never get someone hired is a lack of humility and an overstated sense of self-promotion, so candidates should balance confidence with humility and promote their value to others rather than themselves. Google also values humility, while Oracle's Larry Ellison once hired people who said they were the smartest person they knew."}

{"summary": "The post teases that former contestants of NBC's The Biggest Loser, who lost large amounts of weight through intense daily training on the show, regained much of it afterward, so the weight loss was only temporary."}

{"summary": "The article reviews 20 smartphone apps that encourage getting outdoors, covering trails, wildlife, history, camping, stargazing, geocaching, fishing, skateparks, parkour and more. The clickbait teases the 20 apps to get you out and about, which are these outdoor-focused apps such as Forest XPlorer, ViewRanger, and Star Walk 2."}

{"summary": "The post teases the \"one thing everyone needs\" for a happy, healthy life. According to Harvard's 75-year Grant Study, it is close, intimate, stable relationships, not wealth, fame, or career success. Lonely or isolated people tend to decline sooner and die younger."}

{"summary": "Jessica Simpson wore an all-black outfit with skinny jeans, a low-cut top, blazer and stilettos to a Mexican dinner in Calabasas with fiance Eric Johnson and daughter Maxwell. The post's teaser is her hint about returning to the studio, tweeting \"I need to make music\" after her last album, 2010's Happy Christmas."}

{"summary": "Leann surprised her grandfather Ried with an ultrasound, and he initially missed that she was expecting twins. The real secret teased in the post is that the ultrasound reveals two babies, not one, which makes him sob and swear in excitement."}

{"summary": "The post teases the top buyers of U.S. weapons. According to SIPRI data for 2011-2015, Saudi Arabia was the largest recipient, followed closely by the United Arab Emirates, with Turkey, South Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, Iraq, and Egypt rounding out the top 10."}

{"summary": "Nine-year-old Molly Sings sings Kasey Chambers' song 'Am I Not Pretty Enough?' in her blind audition on The Voice Kids Australia. The judges are moved to tears, and Mel B. wins her over as coach with a girl-power pitch, saying she'd be the best fit for her."}

{"summary": "The post teases that Elizabeth Warren's memoir A Fighting Chance makes the case she should run for president. The article says her book repeatedly echoes fighting-for-the-middle-class themes that point toward a White House bid, despite her public denials, and it points to passages about her past reluctant decisions to take on big fights."}

{"summary": "The post teases the city as Sydney, Australia. LendLease sold all 391 apartments at its Darling Square project on the western edge of the CBD in four hours on a Saturday, with over 400 buyers attending, despite looming oversupply of new apartments."}

{"summary": "Lindsay Lohan posted an Instagram photo from a recording studio with her sister Ali Lohan and Duran Duran's Simon le Bon and Nick Rhodes. The caption says Ali is recording with the band. {"summary": "The tiny plastic tripod in pizza boxes is a \"pizza saver\" that stops the cardboard lid from sagging onto and ripping the cheese. Long Island inventor Carmela Vitale designed it in 1983, patented it in 1985, and never profited from it, letting the patent lapse in 1993."}

{"summary": "The post teases whether people look like their names. The article reports research by Yonat Zwebner and colleagues finding that volunteers shown a headshot and several possible names picked the correct name more often than chance, suggesting people come to resemble their names."}

{"summary": "The article predicts that within 15 years the traditional 9-5 workday will disappear, as millennials prefer flexible schedules, telecommuting, and continuing education, and offices become less essential. It cites a Bentley study where 77% of millennials say flexible hours boost productivity, and a Chinese firm study showing telecommuters were 13% more productive."}

{"summary": "Bob Harper, host of The Biggest Loser, suggests former contestants whose metabolisms have slowed try intermittent fasting, such as skipping breakfast, to offset the hundreds of calories their bodies now burn less. Experts note there's no long-term evidence it works."}

{"summary": "Drake's album \"Views\" has topped the Billboard 200 for nine straight weeks, the longest consecutive streak since Adele's \"21\" in 2012, driven largely by streaming rather than physical sales. It is also the first male artist to do so in over 10 years."}

{"summary": "The post teases #8, which is KFC's BBQ sandwich. A former KFC employee says it's made from chicken too stale to donate to homeless shelters, soaked in BBQ sauce, and kept on a heater for a month. The article lists 12 other fast food items former workers say to avoid, including Taco Bell beans, McDonald's McCafe drinks, and Chipotle's quesarito."}

{"summary": "Glee star Alex Newell, who plays transgender character Wade \"Unique\" Adams on the show, has joined the cast of \"Geography Club,\" a film adaptation of Brent Hartinger's novel. {"summary": "The post is teasing a photo of Alfred Hitchcock wearing a Beatles-style mop-top wig, snapped in 1964 and shared by Retronaut, which the article says resembles Stooge Moe Howard."}

{"summary": "The article reports that Galbani string cheese packaging uses male cartoon cheese characters for its full-fat varieties but a female character for its low-fat version, as noticed by a reader's daughter. The post is teasing that the cheese packaging is sexist in its gender depiction of full-fat versus low-fat products."}

{"summary": "The post teases Eranna, about 60, the last known rat catcher in South India, found in a hilltop Irula area near Denkanikottai, who catches field rats (often to eat) using burrow-smoking techniques. Reporters tracked him down after hearing legends of a tribe that caught and ate rats."}

{"summary": "The post teases the claim that pyramid schemes are secretly legitimate. The article argues that multi-level marketing (MLM) home businesses, often promoted by mothers on social media, are not pyramid schemes and can create real opportunities, comparing their structure to ordinary corporate hierarchies and urging readers to support small business owners."}

{"summary": "Bill Carter, a 25-plus year New York Times TV and media reporter known for books like The Late Shift, is taking a voluntary buyout amid the paper's push to cut 100 staffers. {"summary": "A Gujarat tribal couple from Dahod finally had a tubectomy after having 17 children, 16 daughters and one son. Ramsinh kept trying for another son, and the village persuaded them to stop, citing the difficulty of feeding a large family amid inflation. The teased 'hurry' is the couple's late decision to stop at 17 kids."}

{"summary": "The post teases whether you need to fast before a cholesterol test. The article says no: repeated studies show fasting makes no clinically significant difference to HDL, LDL, or total cholesterol, though it may help measure triglycerides more accurately. Many European guidelines no longer require fasting, and doctors say nonfasting tests are more practical."}

{"summary": "The post is teasing Syracuse University, whose students placed more late-night food orders (10 p.m. to 2 a.m.) than any other school in a GrubHub analysis of over 350 campuses. {"summary": "The post teases the Turing Phone Cadenza, a concept smartphone from California's Turing Robotic Industries running Swordfish OS, with 12GB RAM, 1TB internal storage (expandable via microSD), a 5.8-inch Quad HD display, two Snapdragon 830 processors, a 60MP rear camera, and four SIM slots. It is expected to release next year."}

{"summary": "The post teases a surprise at a shelter, but the article is about orphaned baby genets (a African/European carnivore) found in South Africa after rock-throwing kids drove off their mother. A poodle-cocker spaniel mix named Candy, who wasn't pregnant, began producing milk and nursed and raised them. Two were later released into the wild."}

{"summary": "The post teases a supposed time traveler filming with a cameraphone at a 1995 Mike Tyson fight. The article says no: the camera was an ordinary handheld model widely available in 1995, such as the Casio QV-10A or Logitech Fotoman, and the 'time traveler' is just our biases and hindsight tricking us."}

{"summary": "The post teases the NES Classic Edition's biggest limitation: it cannot connect to the internet or accept external storage, so Nintendo will never add more games beyond its built-in 30 titles, per a statement to Kotaku.
